sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A QUASI-ZONAL LARGE SCALE FLOW REGIME WILL PERSIST OVER THE NORTHERN HALF TO TWO-THIRDS OF THE CONUS THROUGH THE PERIOD. THIS PATTERN WILL BE HIGHLIGHTED BY THE EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD ADVANCEMENT/MODEST AMPLIFICATION OF A POTENT SHORTWAVE TROUGH...FROM THE NORTH-CENTRAL ROCKIES/HIGH PLAINS TO THE MIDWEST/UPPER MS VALLEY BY LATE TONIGHT.

sections.title: CENTRAL PLAINS/MIDWEST/LOWER MO VALLEY
sections.text: INITIALLY...MULTIPLE ONGOING TSTM CLUSTERS AND POTENTIAL MCS/S WILL BE ONGOING THIS MORNING...ONE AREA PROBABLY ACROSS EASTERN KS AND/OR PERHAPS NORTHERN OK/WESTERN MO...IN ADDITION TO A CORRIDOR FROM SD TO SOUTHERN MN/NORTHERN IA. IT IS POSSIBLE THAT SOME OF THIS ACTIVITY COULD POSE A MODEST SEVERE HAIL/WIND THREAT THROUGH THE MORNING...AIDED BY SUSTAINED DUAL SEGMENTS OF A LOW LEVEL JET/ASSOCIATED WARM ADVECTION REGIME. OTHERWISE...A WARM/MOIST AIRMASS WILL ATTEMPT TO RETREAT NORTHEASTWARD ACROSS THE LOWER MO VALLEY/MIDWEST TODAY...AHEAD OF THE APPROACHING/AMPLIFYING MID LEVEL TROUGH AND A MODESTLY DEEPENING SURFACE LOW AND EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD ADVANCING COLD FRONT. OF NOTE...THIS WARM SECTOR RETREAT MAY VERY WELL BE AUGMENTED BY EARLY DAY/ONGOING TSTMS...WHICH PROVIDES LIMITED CERTAINTY ON THE TRUE EXTENT OF AN APPRECIABLE WARM/MOIST SECTOR LATER TODAY. NONETHELESS...IT IS CONCEIVABLE THAT EARLY DAY TSTMS WILL PERSIST THROUGH THE DAY...WITH S/SW PERIPHERAL AND/OR NEAR-COLD FRONTAL SUBSEQUENT DEVELOPMENT BY THIS AFTERNOON WITHIN A RECOVERING/DESTABILIZING BOUNDARY LAYER. sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: AS MENTIONED IN PRIOR OUTLOOKS...SEVERE WEATHER FORECAST UNCERTAINTY IS RELATIVELY HIGH ACROSS THE PLAINS AND MIDDLE MO/MS RIVER VALLEYS THROUGH TONIGHT AS MID LEVEL FLOW STRENGTHENS AND AMPLIFIES OVER THESE AREAS AND STRONGER DESTABILIZATION IS POTENTIALLY LIMITED BY DECAYING OVERNIGHT CONVECTION AND CLOUD COVER. AT LEAST TWO RELATIVELY LOW AMPLITUDE SHORT WAVE TROUGHS ARE EVIDENT IN WATER VAPOR AND RUC DATA THIS MORNING. BOTH OF THESE DISTURBANCES HAVE BEEN AIDING MCS ACTIVITY OVER 1) SD AND MN...AND 2) KS AND MO. MODEL GUIDANCE INDICATES THAT IMPULSE NUMBER 1...NOW MOVING ACROSS WRN SD AND NEB WILL AMPLIFY SUBSTANTIALLY OVER THE NEXT 12H WITH GREATER THAN 60M 500MB HEIGHT FALLS ACROSS IA BY THIS EVENING. IMPULSE NUMBER 2...CONTRIBUTING TO THE KS/MO MCS...IS FORECAST TO REMAIN RELATIVELY LOW IN AMPLITUDE AS IT SPREADS EAST/SOUTHEAST AHEAD OF THE STRONGER AMPLIFICATION OCCURRING OVER IA. DESPITE LOWER AMPLITUDE AND WEAKER HEIGHT FALLS WITH THIS SECOND/SRN DISTURBANCE...DEEP-LAYER ASCENT AND LIFT ALONG/AHEAD OF ADVANCING COLD FRONT...SHOULD OCCUR COINCIDENT WITH GREATER AIRMASS DESTABILIZATION COMPARED TO FARTHER NORTH.

sections.title: IA/MN EWD ACROSS THE MS RIVER TO WRN WI/NRN IL
sections.text: THE SYNOPSIS ABOVE SUGGESTS A BI-MODAL PATTERN TO THE EVOLVING SEVERE WEATHER THREAT LATER TODAY AND THIS IS ALSO THE GENERAL PATTERN DEPICTED IN LATEST MESOSCALE MODELS. POTENTIAL ACROSS THE NRN AREA WILL BE DRIVEN BY STRONG CYCLOGENESIS AND SHEAR OCCURRING AMIDST RELATIVELY LOW CAPE. HOWEVER...VISIBLE IMAGERY IS SHOWING GENERALLY THIN CLOUD COVER ACROSS IA AND EXTREME SWRN MN ATTM AND IT SEEMS REASONABLE TO EXPECT SUFFICIENT SURFACE-BASED DESTABILIZATION FOR SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT LATER TODAY OVER THESE AREAS. STRENGTHENING MID-LEVEL WLY FLOW TO AT LEAST 50KT ATOP GENERALLY SELY/SLY LOW LEVEL FLOW...IN ADDITION TO STRENGTHENING ASCENT ALONG THE WARM FRONT AND NEAR DEEPENING SURFACE LOW...SHOULD SUPPORT AN INCREASING CHANCE FOR ORGANIZED STORMS...INITIALLY IN THE FORM OF SUPERCELLS OR PERHAPS CLUSTERS OF CONVECTION WITH OCCASIONAL EMBEDDED SUPERCELLS. UPSCALE ORGANIZATION TO THE CONVECTION APPEARS QUITE LIKELY AS THE SURFACE LOW CONTINUES TO BECOME BETTER DEFINED ACROSS THIS AREA THROUGH THE EVENING. THIS DEVELOPMENT SHOULD SUPPORT QLCS EVOLUTION WITH MORE INTENSE STORMS AND WIND DAMAGE POTENTIAL SPREADING EAST WITH THE SURFACE LOW...AND ALONG THE WARM FRONT FROM IA/MN INTO SRN

sections.title: KS/MO/NRN OK
sections.text: DEVELOPMENT OF SEVERE WEATHER ACROSS THIS SRN AREA MAY BE DELAYED UNTIL ONGOING MCS ACTIVITY DECAYS FURTHER...OR PERHAPS THE MCS ACTIVITY PERSISTS AND GRADUALLY STRENGTHENS. MOST LIKELY SCENARIO IS THAT MOST ONGOING ACTIVITY CONTINUES TO LOSE INTENSITY OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS BEFORE THE POTENTIAL FOR NEW DEVELOPMENT INCREASES ALONG OUTFLOW BOUNDARY...APPROACHING COLD FRONT...AND SECONDARY WEAK SURFACE LOW NEAR THE INTERSECTION OF THESE BOUNDARIES. MODEST DESTABILIZATION IS LIKELY TO OCCUR COINCIDENT WITH THIS DEVELOPMENT POTENTIAL AND CONVECTION SHOULD BE FUELED BY MLCAPE AOA 2000 J/KG. MAGNITUDE OF INSTABILITY AND STRENGTHENING MID-LEVEL FLOW ACROSS THE AREA SUGGEST THAT SUPERCELLS WITH HAIL ARE POSSIBLE INITIALLY...ESPECIALLY OVER PARTS OF ERN KS. GREATER LOW LEVEL SHEAR AMIDST MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER NEAR THE MCS OUTFLOW...AND ALSO NEAR FRONT/OUTFLOW INTERSECTION SOMEWHERE OVER ERN KS...SUGGEST A GREATER POSSIBILITY OF TORNADOES. SHEAR PROFILES SHOULD BECOME MORE UNIDIRECTIONAL WITH TIME AND LINEAR EVOLUTION IS LIKELY AS THE COLD FRONT MOVES SEWD ACROSS THE AREA TONIGHT. A COUPLE OF STORM CLUSTERS OR LINE SEGMENTS WITH WIND AND HAIL WILL REMAIN A POSSIBILITY ACROSS SERN KS AND ADJA

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A WELL DEFINED UPPER SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL CONTINUE EWD ACROSS THE UPPER MS VALLEY THIS EVENING REACHING THE MIDWESTERN STATES BY THU MORNING. AT THE SURFACE...A COLD FRONT WILL SURGE SEWD ACROSS IA AND MO...BECOMING QUASISTATIONARY ACROSS NRN OK OVERNIGHT. THIS FRONT WILL SERVE AS THE PRIMARY FOCUS FOR CONTINUING CONVECTION THIS EVENING AND OVERNIGHT.

sections.title: KS/OK/MO
sections.text: MULTIPLE SUPERCELLS ARE ONGOING ALONG THE COLD FRONT/OUTFLOW BOUNDARY INTERSECTION ACROSS SERN KS...WITH ADDITIONAL ACTIVITY FILLING IN SWWD ACROSS OK AND INTO THE ERN TX PANHANDLE. THE STORMS ACROSS SERN KS AS WELL AS FAR NERN OK WILL HAVE THE GREATEST THREAT OF TORNADOES AS WELL AS VERY LARGE HAIL. FARTHER SWWD...LOW LEVEL SHEAR DECREASES BUT STRONG INSTABILITY PROFILES AND SHEAR FOR SUPERCELLS WILL STILL FAVOR VERY LARGE HAIL. DAMAGING WINDS GUSTS ARE POSSIBLE WITH ANY CELLS AS WELL. FOR MORE INFORMATION REFERENCE MCD 1841.

sections.title: MN/IA/NRN IL
sections.text: MARGINALLY SEVERE STORMS WITH POSSIBLE HAIL WILL PERSIST ALONG A WARM FRONT FROM SERN MN INTO WRN WI. HOWEVER...THE MAIN THREAT WILL BE WITH ACTIVITY CURRENTLY ALONG THE COLD FRONT AS 0F 01Z...FROM W CNTRL IA INTO EXTREME SERN NEB. THE 00Z OAX SOUNDING SHOWED STEEP MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND STRONG UNIDIRECTIONAL DEEP LAYER SHEAR FOR SUPERCELLS. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS ARE WILL BE POSSIBLE. FARTHER S...THE AIR MASS OVER MUCH OF CNTRL AND ERN MO INTO CNTRL IL HAS NOT RECOVERED FROM EARLIER CONVECTION. HOWEVER...STRONG FORCING ALONG THE FRONT COULD RESULT IN ISOLATED SEVERE HAIL OR WIND OVERNIGHT. ..JEWELL.. 09/16/2010
